additions.reason: The Showbread (lechem hapanim) is the destination concept of the entire parnasa section of Torah #31 — the spiritual level that the ba'al nefesh/Abraham-level person's meals reach. Source lines 37-38, 41-42, 47-48 all use bechina language around it: the ba'al nefesh's meals ARE lechem hapanim (line 37: 'azai beva'dai kol akhilotav use'udotav bechina lechem hapanim'); 'bira' being brought inside IS becoming lechem hapanim (line 48: 'eyilehu lemata, lifnim, sheyihyeh bechina lechem hapanim'). Currently, 'lechem hapanim' appears in Package 4 only implicitly as the telos of the bira/bar umzon chain — but it should be encoded as an explicit node bechina-connected to 'madregat Avraham' and 'ba'al nefesh'. This concept either exists in the dataset under a different spelling or is absent as a ref=31 bechina node.

additions.reason: Hevel peh (the breath/vapor of the mouth) is the vehicle through which nefashot are released and travel through the air to reach other persons. Source lines 35-36, 84: 'vehaKol na'aseh al yedei haHevel pihu, shehu hanefesh' (line 35) and 'Hevel, hu bechina hevel peh, misham yotz'im haneshamot' (line 84). The breath/vapor of the mouth IS the nefesh in the sense that the verbal expression of kisufin = the release of nefesh from potential to actual — the hevel peh is the physical carrier of the soul. This appears in bechina language in the source and belongs in Package 5 (kisufin/nefashot), bechina-connected to 'nefesh' and 'kibur.' It is not currently encoded as a ref=31 bechina edge.

additions.reason: The extra soul of Shabbat (nefesh yeteira) is generated by the very act of yearning for it at the start of Shabbat. Source line 57: 'betchilat haShabbat shetzarich lekabel nefesh yeteira, anu zokhrim me'avedat hanefesh bechol, ve'omrim: vayinafash — vai avdah nefesh, umatchilim lehitga'age'a achareiha. analysis_notes.evil_mirror_observation: Package 8 (Aher/evil) is the evil mirror of Package 6 (lamdan/chasid/tzaddik). Aher is the anti-tzaddik: where the tzaddik is both lamdan AND chasid, Aher is a pure lamdan who rejects the chasid dimension. The mirror structure is exact: lamdan+chasid = malakh Hashem Tzvaot (good); lamdan alone = Mitat alone = Aher who cuts the shoots (evil). Torah #31 presents this as the central structural binary of spiritual life.
analysis_notes.cross_package_observation: The concept 'regalim/regel' appears in two distinct bechina contexts in Torah #31: (1) regalim = parnasa (Package 4: hithalekh = regalim = mamono shel adam), and (2) tefila = regel (Package 6: hatefilah nikret bechina regel). This dual membership reflects the Torah's structural insight: the physical feet that sustain material life (parnasa) and the spiritual standing in prayer both express the same 'regel' quality — the point of contact between the human and the divine, one material, one spiritual. The two are intentionally encoded in different packages to preserve this distinction.
